You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `layout: floorplan` / `|floorplan|` — byte-identical to the original. Walls `|wall|` drawn as a CENTRELINE pen (`draw:` with tagged segments `right(7.2):north`) thickened to poché (`thickness`, default 200 mm; mitred corners), `|partition|`, openings riding a wall's `[ ]`: `|window| { on: north; at: 2.7; width: 1.6 }`, `|door| { on: south; at: 1.05; width: 0.95; swing: left|right; hinge: start|end }` (swing arcs, door leaf; `at` counts along the segment's drawing direction, pen-left is outside), `|stairs| { steps: 14 }`, furniture symbols `|bed|`, `|sofa| { symbol: two }`, `|dining| { symbol: round }`, `|appliance| "F" { symbol: fridge }`, `|bath| { symbol: shower|toilet|sink }` (true-size, rotate/translate in metres), room name text, clear-span dimensions between wall faces (`outer:west-in (-) bathwall:face-out { side: top }` — face anchors `-in`/`-out` on tagged segments; dimension rendering itself may be shared with the drawing-annotation work happening in parallel by another agent: implement what floorplans need in your own module and keep it self-contained), units (`unit: m`, mm), `scale: 0.02` (1:50, px per metre), the >10000 px "'scale:' is a ratio" warning (already implemented in src/drawing.rs), CSS (`.lini-wall`…). The sketch pen, units and drawing layout already exist (src/sketch.rs, src/drawing.rs — walls/partitions are currently thickened outlines without door/window cuts; read the notes at the top of drawing.rs). `executable desugar FILE` shows how these lower (the repo's desugar in src/desugar/drawing.rs reproduces that text).

Test files: /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples prop_hinge, prop_on, prop_steps, prop_swing, prop_thickness (passes now — keep it), skill_08, spec_59, blocks/skill_008, blocks/spec_059; test_samples floorplan.lini, floorplan_parts.lini. Write many synthetic plans in /tmp/<you>/.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-fp/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; start: 171/246) and ensure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmp.py CASEFILE [-o] [-v] [-n N] [-a "args"]
# CASEFILE: snippets separated by lines '----'. Runs the original and ours on
# each; prints OK/FAIL and a short diff. -o: print the original's scene output
# instead. -v: full diff.
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, difflib

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
args = sys.argv[1:]
show_orig = '-o' in args
verbose = '-v' in args
extra = []
nlines = 30
if '-a' in args:
    extra = args[args.index('-a') + 1].split()
if '-n' in args:
    nlines = int(args[args.index('-n') + 1])
path = args[0]
src = open(path).read()
cases = [c.strip('\n') for c in src.split('\n----\n')]
ok = 0
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
for k, c in enumerate(cases):
    if not c.strip():
        continue
    f = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(c + '\n')
    r1 = subprocess.run([ORIG] + extra + ['case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if show_orig:
        print('=== case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
        out = r1.stdout.decode()
        if '<g class="lini-scene">' in out:
            out = out[:out.index('\n') + 1] + out[out.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):]
        sys.stdout.write(r1.stderr.decode())
        sys.stdout.write(out)
        if r1.returncode:
            print('[exit %d]' % r1.returncode)
        continue
    r2 = subprocess.run([MINE] + extra + ['case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=30)
    same = r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode
    if same:
        ok += 1
        print('OK   case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
        continue
    print('FAIL case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
    a = (r1.stderr.decode() + r1.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r1.returncode).split('\n')
    b = (r2.stderr.decode() + r2.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r2.returncode).split('\n')
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, 'orig', 'mine', n=0, lineterm=''))
    for l in diff[2:(None if verbose else nlines)]:
        print('   ' + l[:400])
if not show_orig:
    print('%d / %d OK' % (ok, len([c for c in cases if c.strip()])))

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

// Registry order is the order type rules are emitted in the stylesheet.
pub static TYPES: &[TypeDef] = &[
    t!("block", Block, None, "fill: none; stroke: none; stroke-width: 2; padding: 0; gap: 36;"),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Run the original on a generated snippet and return stdout/stderr.
import subprocess, os, tempfile, sys, re

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
_d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')


def run(src, args=(), exe=ORIG):
    f = os.path.join(_d, 'p.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + list(args) + ['p.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=_d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode(), r.returncode


def scene(out):
    if '<g class="lini-scene">' in out:
        return out[out.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):]
    return out

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmp.py CASEFILE [-o] [-v] [-n N] [-a "args"]
# CASEFILE: snippets separated by lines '----'. Runs the original and ours on
# each; prints OK/FAIL and a short diff. -o: print the original's scene output
# instead. -v: full diff.
import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, difflib

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
args = sys.argv[1:]
show_orig = '-o' in args
verbose = '-v' in args
extra = []
nlines = 30
if '-a' in args:
    extra = args[args.index('-a') + 1].split()
if '-n' in args:
    nlines = int(args[args.index('-n') + 1])
path = args[0]
src = open(path).read()
cases = [c.strip('\n') for c in src.split('\n----\n')]
ok = 0
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
for k, c in enumerate(cases):
    if not c.strip():
        continue
    f = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(c + '\n')
    r1 = subprocess.run([ORIG] + extra + ['case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if show_orig:
        print('=== case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
        out = r1.stdout.decode()
        if '<g class="lini-scene">' in out:
            out = out[:out.index('\n') + 1] + out[out.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):]
        sys.stdout.write(r1.stderr.decode())
        sys.stdout.write(out)
        if r1.returncode:
            print('[exit %d]' % r1.returncode)
        continue
    r2 = subprocess.run([MINE] + extra + ['case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=30)
    same = r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode
    if same:
        ok += 1
        print('OK   case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
        continue
    print('FAIL case %d: %s' % (k, c.split('\n')[0][:100]))
    a = (r1.stderr.decode() + r1.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r1.returncode).split('\n')
    b = (r2.stderr.decode() + r2.stdout.decode() + '[exit %d]' % r2.returncode).split('\n')
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, 'orig', 'mine', n=0, lineterm=''))
    for l in diff[2:(None if verbose else nlines)]:
        print('   ' + l[:400])
if not show_orig:
    print('%d / %d OK' % (ok, len([c for c in cases if c.strip()])))
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Run the original on a generated snippet and return stdout/stderr.
import subprocess, os, tempfile, sys, re

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
_d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')


def run(src, args=(), exe=ORIG):
    f = os.path.join(_d, 'p.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + list(args) + ['p.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=_d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode(), r.returncode


def scene(out):
    if '<g class="lini-scene">' in out:
        return out[out.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):]
    return out

from probe import run, scene

# usage: halo2.py P Q SW [end]
# Bisect the smallest distance from the tip at which a crossing's halo is kept.
P = sys.argv[1]
Q = sys.argv[2]
SW = sys.argv[3]
END = len(sys.argv) > 4 and sys.argv[4] == 'end'
RW = sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else '0.01'


def mk(extra):
    return '''{ layout: floorplan; unit: m; scale: 0.02 }
|wall#o| { draw: move(-2, -2) right(9):n down(8):e left(9):s close():w; }
|sofa#p| { symbol: stool; translate: %s }
|sofa#q| { symbol: stool; translate: %s }
%s
p (-) q
''' % (P, Q, extra)


o, e, c = run(mk(''))
s = scene(o)
mk_ = re.findall(r'lini-marker-dim lini-poly" transform="[^"]*">\n\s*<polygon points="([^"]*)"', s)
t1 = tuple(map(float, mk_[0].split()[0].split(',')))
t2 = tuple(map(float, mk_[1].split()[0].split(',')))
L = math.hypot(t2[0] - t1[0], t2[1] - t1[1])
d = ((t2[0] - t1[0]) / L, (t2[1] - t1[1]) / L)
print('tips', t1, t2, 'L', L, 'd', d)


def halos(s0):
    px = t1[0] + d[0] * s0
    py = t1[1] + d[1] * s0
    ex = '|rect| { width: %s; height: 0.6; translate: %.8f %.8f; fill: none; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: %s }' % (RW, px / 80, py / 80, SW)
    o, e, c = run(mk(ex))
    s = scene(o)
    m = re.search(r'lini-dim-line lini-line" transform="[^"]*">\n(\s*<mask.*)', s)
    return re.findall(r'points="([^"]*)"', m.group(1)) if m else []


if END:
    lo, hi = L - 40.0, L - 5.0   # hi: dropped (near the end), lo: kept
    assert halos(lo), 'lo should keep'
    for _ in range(30):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if halos(mid):
            lo = mid

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Run every scratch case file (t*.txt, c*.txt, d*.txt, al*.txt, k*.lini) and
# print a compact OK/FAIL map, so behaviour changes can be diffed.
import glob, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
files = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/fp/t*.txt') + glob.glob('/tmp/fp/c*.txt') + glob.glob('/tmp/fp/d*.txt') + glob.glob('/tmp/fp/al*.txt') + glob.glob('/tmp/fp/k*.lini'))
res = []
tot = ok = 0
for f in files:
    src = open(f).read()
    cases = [c.strip('\n') for c in src.split('\n----\n')] if f.endswith('.txt') else [src]
    marks = ''
    for c in cases:
        if not c.strip():
            continue
        p = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
        open(p, 'w').write(c + '\n')
        r1 = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
        r2 = subprocess.run([MINE, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=30)
        same = r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode
        marks += '.' if same else 'F'
        tot += 1
        ok += same
    res.append('%s %s' % (os.path.basename(f), marks))
out = '\n'.join(res)
print(out)
print('TOTAL %d / %d' % (ok, tot))
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    open(sys.argv[1], 'w').write(out + '\n')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Aligned dimensions: random fixtures, slanted walls, rotated beds; dims
# between points, faces and sides, mixed with axis dims. Compare original
# and ours; failures → /tmp/fp/fuzz3_fail.txt
import random, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 50
rnd = random.Random(seed)

FIX = {
    'bed': ['queen', 'king', 'double', 'single'],
    'sofa': ['three', 'two', 'one', 'stool'],
    'dining': ['six', 'four', 'round'],
    'bath': ['tub', 'shower', 'toilet', 'sink'],
    'appliance': ['stove', 'fridge', 'washer', 'dishwasher'],
}


def num(v):
    return ('%.2f' % v).rstrip('0').rstrip('.')


def plan():
    out = []
    scale = rnd.choice(['0.02', '0.02', '0.01', '0.04'])
    out.append('{ layout: floorplan; unit: m; scale: %s }' % scale)
    W = rnd.randint(40, 80) / 10
    H = rnd.randint(30, 60) / 10
    out.append('|wall#o| { draw: move(0, 0) right(%s):n down(%s):e left(%s):s close():w; }' % (num(W), num(H), num(W)))
    names = []
    faces = []   # (name, slant key)
    # slanted walls: pairs of parallel runs
    for k in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
        dx = rnd.choice([1, 2, -1, 1.5, 0.5])
        dy = rnd.choice([1, -1, 2, 0.5, -1.5])
        x0 = rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 25) / 10
        y0 = rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 15) / 10
        out.append('|wall#s%d| { draw: move(%s, %s) line(%s, %s):f; }' % (k, num(x0), num(y0), num(dx), num(dy)))
        faces.append(('s%d' % k, (dx, dy)))
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            off = rnd.choice([0.8, 1.2, -1, 1.5])
            sc = rnd.choice([1, 0.5, 1.5])
            out.append('|wall#t%d| { draw: move(%s, %s) line(%s, %s):f; }' % (k, num(x0 + off), num(y0), num(dx * sc), num(dy * sc)))
            faces.append(('t%d' % k, (dx, dy)))
    for k in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)):
        fam = rnd.choice(list(FIX))
        sym = rnd.choice(FIX[fam])
        props = ['symbol: %s' % sym]
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            props.append('rotate: %d' % rnd.choice([30, 45, -30, 60, 90]))
        props.append('translate: %s %s' % (num(rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 5) / 10), num(rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 5) / 10)))
        out.append('|%s#n%d| { %s }' % (fam, k, '; '.join(props)))
        names.append('n%d' % k)
    anchors = ['', '', ':center', ':top-left', ':bottom-right', ':top-right']
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 5)):
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.55 or not faces:
            a, b = rnd.sample(names, 2)
            l = '%s%s (-) %s%s' % (a, rnd.choice(anchors), b, rnd.choice(anchors))
        elif r < 0.8:
            # parallel faces
            same = [f for f in faces]
            fa = rnd.choice(same)
            par = [f for f in faces if f[1][0] * fa[1][1] - f[1][1] * fa[1][0] == 0 and f[0] != fa[0]]
            if par:
                fb = rnd.choice(par)
                l = '%s:f (-) %s:f' % (fa[0], fb[0])
            else:
                l = '%s:f (-) %s' % (fa[0], rnd.choice(names))
        else:
            fa = rnd.choice(faces)
            l = '%s (-) %s:f' % (rnd.choice(names), fa[0])
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            l += rnd.choice([' { side: left }', ' { side: right }'])
        if rnd.random() < 0.15:
            l = l.replace(' (-) ', ' (-) ', 1) + ''
            l += ' "%s"' % rnd.choice(['x', 'clear', 'a longer label'])
        out.append(l)
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        out.append(rnd.choice(['o:w-in (-) o:e-in { side: top }', 'o:n-in (-) o:s-in', 'o:w-out (-) o:e-out', 'o:n-in (-) o:s-in { side: left }']))
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n'


ok = 0
fails = []
for k in range(n):
    src = plan()
    f = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(src)
    r1 = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([MINE, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode:
        ok += 1
    else:
        fails.append(src)
print('OK %d / %d' % (ok, n))
if fails:
    open('/tmp/fp/fuzz3_fail.txt', 'w').write('\n----\n'.join(fails))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Parse the dimension elements (ext, ext, line, marker, marker, text) out of
# the original's and our output for a lini file and print them side by side.
import sys, re, subprocess, os

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'


def parse(svg):
    s = svg[svg.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):] if '<g class="lini-scene">' in svg else svg
    items = []
    pat = re.compile(r'<g class="lini-node (lini-ext-line|lini-dim-line|lini-marker lini-marker-dim)[^"]*"[^>]*>\n(?:\s*<mask[^\n]*\n)?\s*<(line|polygon) ([^/]*)/>|<text class="lini-text lini-dim-text" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<')
    for m in pat.finditer(s):
        if m.group(1):
            kind = {'lini-ext-line': 'ext', 'lini-dim-line': 'line'}.get(m.group(1), 'mark')
            attrs = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', m.group(3)))
            if kind == 'mark':
                v = attrs['points'].split()[0]
            else:
                v = '%s,%s>%s,%s' % (attrs['x1'], attrs['y1'], attrs['x2'], attrs['y2'])
            items.append((kind, v))
        else:
            items.append(('text', '%s,%s %s' % (m.group(4), m.group(5), m.group(6))))
    return items


f = sys.argv[1]
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f))
b = os.path.basename(f)
o = subprocess.run([ORIG, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
m = subprocess.run([MINE, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
po, pm = parse(o), parse(m)
for k in range(max(len(po), len(pm))):
    a = po[k] if k < len(po) else ('', '')
    c = pm[k] if k < len(pm) else ('', '')
    flag = '  ' if a == c else '!!'
    print('%s %-5s %-40s | %-40s' % (flag, a[0], a[1], c[1]))

import sys, re, math, subprocess, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/scripts')
from tw import tw

f = sys.argv[1]
D = int(sys.argv[2])
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f))
o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', os.path.basename(f)], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
s = o[o.index('<g class="lini-scene">'):]
pat = re.compile(r'<g class="lini-node (lini-ext-line|lini-dim-line|lini-marker lini-marker-dim)[^"]*"[^>]*>\n(?:\s*<mask[^\n]*\n)?\s*<(line|polygon) ([^/]*)/>|<text class="lini-text lini-dim-text" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*?(?:rotate\(([^ ]*) [^>]*)?>([^<]*)<')
items = []
for m in pat.finditer(s):
    if m.group(1):
        kind = {'lini-ext-line': 'ext', 'lini-dim-line': 'line'}.get(m.group(1), 'mark')
        attrs = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', m.group(3)))
        if kind == 'mark':
            v = [tuple(map(float, q.split(','))) for q in attrs['points'].split()]
        else:
            v = [(float(attrs['x1']), float(attrs['y1'])), (float(attrs['x2']), float(attrs['y2']))]
        items.append((kind, v))
    else:
        items.append(('text', (float(m.group(4)), float(m.group(5)), float(m.group(6) or 0), m.group(7))))
dims = [items[k:k + 6] for k in range(0, len(items), 6)]


def dot(a, b):
    return a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1]


def geo(dm):
    e1, e2, ln, m1, m2, tx = dm
    t_lo, t_hi = m1[1][0], m2[1][0]
    rot = tx[1][2]
    r = (math.cos(math.radians(rot)), math.sin(math.radians(rot)))
    up = (r[1], -r[0])
    return e1[1], e2[1], ln[1], m1[1], m2[1], tx[1], r, up


g = geo(dims[D])
e1 = g[0]
# D's outward: along its first ext line
v = (e1[1][0] - e1[0][0], e1[1][1] - e1[0][1])
L = math.hypot(*v)
oD = (v[0] / L, v[1] / L)
anchor = (e1[0][0] - 3 * oD[0], e1[0][1] - 3 * oD[1])
base = dot(anchor, oD)
tip = g[3][0]
pos = dot(tip, oD)
print('D', D, 'oD', oD, 'pos - base', pos - base)
for k in range(D):
    e1, e2, ln, m1, m2, tx, r, up = geo(dims[k])
    w = tw(tx[3], 12, 400)
    pts = {}
    pts['line'] = ln
    pts['marks'] = m1 + m2
    pts['ext_far'] = [e1[1], e2[1]]
    pts['ext_all'] = e1 + e2
    c, sn = abs(r[0]), abs(r[1])
    hw = w / 2 * c + 6 * sn
    hh = w / 2 * sn + 6 * c
    pts['text_aabb'] = [(tx[0] + a * hw, tx[1] + b * hh) for a in (-1, 1) for b in (-1, 1)]
    pts['text_rect'] = [(tx[0] + a * w / 2 * r[0] + b * 6 * up[0], tx[1] + a * w / 2 * r[1] + b * 6 * up[1]) for a in (-1, 1) for b in (-1, 1)]

    c0 = min(dot(q, up) for q in allp)
    c1 = max(dot(q, up) for q in allp)
    band = [(r[0] * a + up[0] * cc, r[1] * a + up[1] * cc) for a in (a0, a1) for cc in (c0, c1)]
    pts['band'] = band
    out = []

import sys, re, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/fp')
from probe import run, scene

# A dim line between p and q crossing the left edge of a tall thin rect at
# a shallow angle; report the halo on the dim line.
def mk(ang, sw):
    # p at (100, 100); q along angle `ang` (deg from vertical), 200 px away
    a = math.radians(ang)
    p = (100.0, 100.0)
    q = (p[0] + 200 * math.sin(a), p[1] + 200 * math.cos(a))
    # rect left edge crosses the line (the line will be offset by 20/32;
    # put the rect wide so the crossing is with its left edge)
    return '''{ layout: floorplan; unit: m; scale: 0.02 }
|wall#o| { draw: move(-3, -3) right(10):n down(10):e left(10):s close():w; }
|sofa#p| { symbol: stool; translate: %.6f %.6f }
|sofa#q| { symbol: stool; translate: %.6f %.6f }
|rect#r| { width: 1; height: 3; translate: %.6f %.6f; fill: none; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: %s }
p (-) q { side: left }
''' % (p[0] / 80, p[1] / 80, q[0] / 80, q[1] / 80, 0, 0, sw)


for ang in [float(x) for x in sys.argv[2:]]:
    sw = sys.argv[1]
    src = mk(ang, sw)
    o = run(src)[0]
    s = scene(o)
    ln = re.search(r'lini-dim-line lini-line" [^>]*>\n(\s*<mask[^\n]*\n)?\s*<line x1="([^"]*)" y1="([^"]*)" x2="([^"]*)" y2="([^"]*)"', s)
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = map(float, ln.group(2, 3, 4, 5))
    # place the rect so its left edge is crossed at the line's middle
    t = 0.5
    cx, cy = x1 + (x2 - x1) * t, y1 + (y2 - y1) * t
    src2 = src.replace('translate: 0.000000 0.000000', 'translate: %.6f %.6f' % ((cx + 40) / 80, cy / 80))
    o2 = run(src2)[0]
    s2 = scene(o2)
    ln2 = re.search(r'lini-dim-line lini-line" [^>]*>\n(\s*<mask[^\n]*\n)?\s*<line', s2)
    halos = re.findall(r'points="([^"]*)"', ln2.group(1) or '')
    d = (x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
    L = math.hypot(*d)
    sn = abs(d[0]) / L
    print('ang %.2f sin %.4f half %.2f' % (ang, sn, (float(sw) / 2 + 2) / sn), halos)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Floor plans in the style of the samples: defines (|slab::rect|,
# |room::block|), a shell with tagged runs, partitions with doors, slabs,
# fixtures with labels, room names, a north arrow, and face dimensions.
# Failures → /tmp/fp/fuzz4_fail.txt
import random, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 30
rnd = random.Random(seed)

FIX = {
    'bed': ['queen', 'king', 'double', 'single'],
    'sofa': ['three', 'two', 'one', 'corner', 'stool'],
    'dining': ['six', 'four', 'round'],
    'bath': ['tub', 'shower', 'toilet', 'sink', 'double-sink'],
    'appliance': ['stove', 'fridge', 'washer', 'dishwasher'],
}


def num(v):
    return ('%.2f' % v).rstrip('0').rstrip('.')


def plan():
    out = []
    out.append('{')
    out.append('  density: %s;' % rnd.choice(['4', '4', '3']))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        out.append('  font-size: %s;' % rnd.choice(['10', '11', '13']))
    out.append('  |slab::rect| { fill: --bg; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: 1; }')
    out.append('  |room::block| { layout: flow; direction: column; align: center; gap: 2; font-size: 11; letter-spacing: %s; }' % rnd.choice(['0', '1']))
    out.append('}')
    title = rnd.choice(['', '"UNIT 1" ', '"FLAT — 40 m²" '])
    unit = rnd.choice(['m', 'm', 'mm'])
    k = 1000 if unit == 'mm' else 1
    out.append('|floorplan#u| %s{ unit: %s; scale: %s; } [' % (title, unit, rnd.choice(['0.02', '0.02', '0.025'])))
    W = rnd.randint(60, 110) / 10
    H = rnd.randint(45, 75) / 10

    def u(v):
        return num(v * k)
    out.append('  |wall#outer| { draw: move(0, 0) right(%s):north down(%s):east left(%s):south close():west; } [' % (u(W), u(H), u(W)))
    used = {'north': [], 'east': [], 'south': [], 'west': []}
    lens = {'north': W, 'east': H, 'south': W, 'west': H}
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 4)):
        s = rnd.choice(list(lens))
        L = lens[s]
        wd = rnd.choice([0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.2, 1.6, 2])
        if wd > L - 0.4:
            continue
        at = rnd.randint(2, int((L - wd) * 10) - 2) / 10
        if any(not (at + wd <= a0 - 0.1 or at >= a1 + 0.1) for (a0, a1) in used[s]):
            continue
        used[s].append((at, at + wd))
        kind = rnd.choice(['door', 'window', 'window'])
        lab = rnd.choice(['', '"D1" ', '"W2" '])
        props = ['on: %s' % s, 'at: %s' % u(at), 'width: %s' % u(wd)]
        if kind == 'door':
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                props.append('symbol: sliding')
            elif rnd.random() < 0.5:
                props.append('swing: %s' % rnd.choice(['left', 'right']))
            if rnd.random() < 0.3 and 'symbol: sliding' not in props:
                props.append('hinge: end')
        out.append('    |%s| %s{ %s; }' % (kind, lab, '; '.join(props)))
    out.append('  ]')
    parts = []
    for pi in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
        x = rnd.randint(15, int(W * 10) - 15) / 10
        y = rnd.randint(15, int(H * 10) - 15) / 10
        name = 'p%d' % pi
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            out.append('  |partition#%s| { draw: move(%s, 0) down(%s):side; } [' % (name, u(x), u(y)))
            parts.append((name, 'side', 'v'))
            if y > 1.3 and rnd.random() < 0.7:
                out.append('    |door| "D%d" { on: side; at: %s; width: %s; swing: %s; }' % (pi + 3, u(0.2), u(min(0.9, y - 0.4)), rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
        else:
            out.append('  |partition#%s| { draw: move(0, %s) right(%s):head down(%s):side; } [' % (name, u(y), u(x), u(H - y)))
            parts.append((name, 'head', 'h'))
            parts.append((name, 'side', 'v'))
            if H - y > 1.3 and rnd.random() < 0.7:
                out.append('    |door| { on: side; at: %s; width: %s; }' % (u(0.3), u(min(0.9, H - y - 0.5))))
        out.append('  ]')
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 3)):
        out.append('  |slab| { width: %s; height: %s; translate: %s %s;%s }' % (
            u(rnd.randint(4, 20) / 10), u(rnd.randint(4, 15) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 5) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 5) / 10),
            rnd.choice(['', '', ' radius: 4;'])))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 6)):
        fam = rnd.choice(list(FIX))
        props = []
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            props.append('symbol: %s' % rnd.choice(FIX[fam]))
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            props.append('rotate: %d' % rnd.choice([90, 180, 270]))
        props.append('translate: %s %s' % (u(rnd.randint(6, int(W * 10) - 6) / 10), u(rnd.randint(6, int(H * 10) - 6) / 10)))
        lab = rnd.choice(['', '', '"F" ', '"W/D" ', '"queen" '])
        out.append('  |%s| %s{ %s; }' % (fam, lab, '; '.join(props)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        out.append('  |stairs| %s{ steps: %d; translate: %s %s;%s }' % (rnd.choice(['', '"UP" ']), rnd.randint(4, 12), u(W / 2), u(H / 2), rnd.choice(['', ' rotate: 90;'])))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        out.append('  |room| { translate: %s %s; } [ "%s"%s ]' % (u(rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 5) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 5) / 10),
                                                              rnd.choice(['LIVING', 'BED', 'BATH', 'KITCHEN / DINING']), rnd.choice(['', ' "12.5 m²"'])))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        out.append('  |sketch#north| { draw: move(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) close(); fill: --stroke-dark; stroke: none; }' % (
            u(-0.8), u(H - 1), u(0.22), u(0.72), u(-0.22), u(-0.2), u(-0.22), u(0.2)))
    dims = ['outer:west-in (-) outer:east-in { side: top; }', 'outer:north-in (-) outer:south-in { side: right; }',
            'outer:west-out (-) outer:east-out { side: bottom; }', 'outer:north-out (-) outer:south-out { side: left; }']
    for (nm, seg, o) in parts:
        if o == 'v':
            dims.append('outer:west-in (-) %s:%s-out { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['top', 'bottom'])))
            dims.append('%s:%s-in (-) outer:east-in { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['top', 'bottom'])))
        else:
            dims.append('outer:north-in (-) %s:%s-out { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
            dims.append('%s:%s-in (-) outer:south-in { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
    rnd.shuffle(dims)
    for dm in dims[:rnd.randint(1, len(dims))]:
        out.append('  ' + dm)
    out.append(']')
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n'


ok = 0
fails = []
for _ in range(n):
    src = plan()
    f = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(src)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Floor plans in the style of the samples: defines (|slab::rect|,
# |room::block|), a shell with tagged runs, partitions with doors, slabs,
# fixtures with labels, room names, a north arrow, and face dimensions.
# Failures → /tmp/fp/fuzz4_fail.txt
import random, subprocess, os, sys, tempfile

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/bin-fp/executable'
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/fp')
seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 30
rnd = random.Random(seed)

FIX = {
    'bed': ['queen', 'king', 'double', 'single'],
    'sofa': ['three', 'two', 'one', 'corner', 'stool'],
    'dining': ['six', 'four', 'round'],
    'bath': ['tub', 'shower', 'toilet', 'sink', 'double-sink'],
    'appliance': ['stove', 'fridge', 'washer', 'dishwasher'],
}


def num(v):
    return ('%.2f' % v).rstrip('0').rstrip('.')


def plan():
    out = []
    out.append('{')
    out.append('  density: %s;' % rnd.choice(['4', '4', '3']))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        out.append('  font-size: %s;' % rnd.choice(['10', '11', '13']))
    out.append('  |slab::rect| { fill: --bg; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: 1; }')
    out.append('  |room::block| { layout: flow; direction: column; align: center; gap: 2; font-size: 11; letter-spacing: %s; }' % rnd.choice(['0', '1']))
    out.append('}')
    title = rnd.choice(['', '"UNIT 1" ', '"FLAT — 40 m²" '])
    unit = rnd.choice(['m', 'm', 'mm'])
    k = 1000 if unit == 'mm' else 1
    out.append('|floorplan#u| %s{ unit: %s; scale: %s; } [' % (title, unit, rnd.choice(['0.02', '0.02', '0.025'])))
    W = rnd.randint(60, 110) / 10
    H = rnd.randint(45, 75) / 10

    def u(v):
        return num(v * k)
    out.append('  |wall#outer| { draw: move(0, 0) right(%s):north down(%s):east left(%s):south close():west; } [' % (u(W), u(H), u(W)))
    used = {'north': [], 'east': [], 'south': [], 'west': []}
    lens = {'north': W, 'east': H, 'south': W, 'west': H}
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 4)):
        s = rnd.choice(list(lens))
        L = lens[s]
        wd = rnd.choice([0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.2, 1.6, 2])
        if wd > L - 0.4:
            continue
        at = rnd.randint(2, int((L - wd) * 10) - 2) / 10
        if any(not (at + wd <= a0 - 0.1 or at >= a1 + 0.1) for (a0, a1) in used[s]):
            continue
        used[s].append((at, at + wd))
        kind = rnd.choice(['door', 'window', 'window'])
        lab = rnd.choice(['', '"D1" ', '"W2" '])
        props = ['on: %s' % s, 'at: %s' % u(at), 'width: %s' % u(wd)]
        if kind == 'door':
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                props.append('symbol: sliding')
            elif rnd.random() < 0.5:
                props.append('swing: %s' % rnd.choice(['left', 'right']))
            if rnd.random() < 0.3 and 'symbol: sliding' not in props:
                props.append('hinge: end')
        out.append('    |%s| %s{ %s; }' % (kind, lab, '; '.join(props)))
    out.append('  ]')
    parts = []
    for pi in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
        x = rnd.randint(15, int(W * 10) - 15) / 10
        y = rnd.randint(15, int(H * 10) - 15) / 10
        name = 'p%d' % pi
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            out.append('  |partition#%s| { draw: move(%s, 0) down(%s):side; } [' % (name, u(x), u(y)))
            parts.append((name, 'side', 'v'))
            if y > 1.3 and rnd.random() < 0.7:
                out.append('    |door| "D%d" { on: side; at: %s; width: %s; swing: %s; }' % (pi + 3, u(0.2), u(min(0.9, y - 0.4)), rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
        else:
            out.append('  |partition#%s| { draw: move(0, %s) right(%s):head down(%s):side; } [' % (name, u(y), u(x), u(H - y)))
            parts.append((name, 'head', 'h'))
            parts.append((name, 'side', 'v'))
            if H - y > 1.3 and rnd.random() < 0.7:
                out.append('    |door| { on: side; at: %s; width: %s; }' % (u(0.3), u(min(0.9, H - y - 0.5))))
        out.append('  ]')
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 3)):
        out.append('  |slab| { width: %s; height: %s; translate: %s %s;%s }' % (
            u(rnd.randint(4, 20) / 10), u(rnd.randint(4, 15) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 5) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 5) / 10),
            rnd.choice(['', '', ' radius: 4;'])))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 6)):
        fam = rnd.choice(list(FIX))
        props = []
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            props.append('symbol: %s' % rnd.choice(FIX[fam]))
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            props.append('rotate: %d' % rnd.choice([90, 180, 270]))
        props.append('translate: %s %s' % (u(rnd.randint(6, int(W * 10) - 6) / 10), u(rnd.randint(6, int(H * 10) - 6) / 10)))
        lab = rnd.choice(['', '', '"F" ', '"W/D" ', '"queen" '])
        out.append('  |%s| %s{ %s; }' % (fam, lab, '; '.join(props)))
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        out.append('  |stairs| %s{ steps: %d; translate: %s %s;%s }' % (rnd.choice(['', '"UP" ']), rnd.randint(4, 12), u(W / 2), u(H / 2), rnd.choice(['', ' rotate: 90;'])))
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        out.append('  |room| { translate: %s %s; } [ "%s"%s ]' % (u(rnd.randint(5, int(W * 10) - 5) / 10), u(rnd.randint(5, int(H * 10) - 5) / 10),
                                                              rnd.choice(['LIVING', 'BED', 'BATH', 'KITCHEN / DINING']), rnd.choice(['', ' "12.5 m²"'])))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        out.append('  |sketch#north| { draw: move(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) line(%s, %s) close(); fill: --stroke-dark; stroke: none; }' % (
            u(-0.8), u(H - 1), u(0.22), u(0.72), u(-0.22), u(-0.2), u(-0.22), u(0.2)))
    dims = ['outer:west-in (-) outer:east-in { side: top; }', 'outer:north-in (-) outer:south-in { side: right; }',
            'outer:west-out (-) outer:east-out { side: bottom; }', 'outer:north-out (-) outer:south-out { side: left; }']
    for (nm, seg, o) in parts:
        if o == 'v':
            dims.append('outer:west-in (-) %s:%s-out { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['top', 'bottom'])))
            dims.append('%s:%s-in (-) outer:east-in { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['top', 'bottom'])))
        else:
            dims.append('outer:north-in (-) %s:%s-out { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
            dims.append('%s:%s-in (-) outer:south-in { side: %s; }' % (nm, seg, rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])))
    rnd.shuffle(dims)
    for dm in dims[:rnd.randint(1, len(dims))]:
        out.append('  ' + dm)
    out.append(']')
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n'


ok = 0
fails = []
for _ in range(n):
    src = plan()
    f = os.path.join(d, 'case.lini')
    open(f, 'w').write(src)
    r1 = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([MINE, 'case.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode:
        ok += 1
    else:
        fails.append(src)
print('OK %d / %d' % (ok, n))
if fails:
    open('/tmp/fp/fuzz4_fail.txt', 'w').write('\n----\n'.join(fails))

from probe import run, scene

# p, q: rects at fixed centres; p (-) q aligned; ext line from p's centre
# leaves p's box through its top. Vary p's height and report halos on the
# first ext line.
def mk(h, w=0.6, sw=1):
    return '''{ layout: floorplan; unit: m; scale: 0.02 }
|wall#o| { draw: move(-2, -2) right(9):n down(8):e left(9):s close():w; }
|rect#p| { width: %s; height: %.6f; translate: 1 2; fill: none; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: %s }
|rect#q| { width: 0.3; height: 0.3; translate: 3 2.6; fill: none; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: 1 }
p (-) q { side: left }
''' % (w, h, sw)


for h in [float(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]]:
    o = run(mk(h))[0]
    s = scene(o)
    m = re.search(r'lini-ext-line lini-line" [^>]*>\n(\s*<mask[^\n]*\n)?\s*<line x1="([^"]*)" y1="([^"]*)" x2="([^"]*)" y2="([^"]*)"', s)
    halos = re.findall(r'points="([^"]*)"', m.group(1) or '')
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = map(float, m.group(2, 3, 4, 5))
    u = (x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
    L = math.hypot(*u)
    u = (u[0] / L, u[1] / L)
    # exit through the top: y = 160 - h*40
    top = 160 - h * 40
    s_exit = (top - y1) / u[1] if u[1] != 0 else None
    print('h %.4f exit at s=%.3f' % (h, s_exit), halos, [round(((float(p.split()[0].split(',')[0]) - x1) * u[0] + (float(p.split()[0].split(',')[1]) - y1) * u[1]), 3) for p in halos])

2	// vocabulary.
3	//
4	// - `|wall|` / `|partition|` are sketches whose `draw:` is the CENTRELINE;
5	//   `outline()` thickens it into the poché (mitred joints, bevelled past

7	// - `|door|` / `|window|` ride their wall's `[ ]`: `on:` names a straight
8	//   tagged segment, `at:` stations the opening along the segment's drawing
9	//   direction, `width:` (900 / 1200 mm) its gap. The opening is a block on
10	//   the gap (rotated to the run) drawing its leaf + quarter swing arc
11	//   (`swing:` left|right of the pen's travel, `hinge:` start|end), two leaves
12	//   for `double`, two panels for `sliding`, or a window's sill pair.
13	// - `|stairs|` and the fixture families (`|bed|`, `|sofa|`, `|dining|`,
14	//   `|bath|`, `|appliance|`) draw true-size symbol bodies as one path,
15	//   stretched by an explicit width / height; a label reads beside the body
16	//   (an appliance's inside it).

- **For the drawing-annotation work:** the cut-out rules I worked out should also apply to drawings:
  - crossings shallower than sin 0.1 are ignored;
  - gaps merge in crossing order;
  - no cut-out opens under any arrowhead laid so far (its box grown by half the line's stroke);
  - box corners take the wider of the two sides' cut-outs;
  - layout containers are not obstacles.

  The module header in `floorplan.rs` documents these.
